item.title: Nuclear experts urge Trump not to let Iran steer talks away from regime's atomic threat
item.description: Nuclear experts urged President Trump to keep Iran’s nuclear program at the center of talks, warning Tehran could seek sanctions relief before addressing its remaining nuclear capabilities.
item.content:encoded:
Iran’s top Revolutionary Guard commander declared Wednesday that Tehran would continue working on nuclear weapons as long as the United States and Israel possess them, intensifying concerns that Iran is using negotiations over the Strait of Hormuz to postpone concessions on its nuclear program.

"As long as the United States and Israel possess nuclear weapons, we will continue working on them for our national security," IRGC commander-in-chief Ahmad Vahidi said, according to a translation of remarks circulating Wednesday. "If they disarm, we will disarm."

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu responded by vowing that Israel would continue preventing Iran from obtaining a nuclear weapon, with or without a diplomatic agreement.

WHO IS AHMAD VAHIDI? IRAN’S NEW IRGC CHIEF TIED TO GLOBAL ATTACKS AND ‘DEATH TO AMERICA’ IDEOLOGY

"Today, we heard the commander of the Revolutionary Guards, Vahidi, explicitly declare Iran’s intention to continue developing nuclear weapons — ‘continue,’ as he put it," Netanyahu said at a ceremony marking the reinterment of Shimon and Rivka Herzl, the grandparents of the founder of modern day Zionism, Theodor Herzl.

"Well, as prime minister of Israel, I too am determined to continue — to continue preventing Iran from possessing nuclear weapons," he said.

Netanyahu praised President Donald Trump as Israel’s greatest friend in the White House and expressed appreciation for the two countries’ joint efforts against Iran’s nuclear ambitions.

"Israel’s existence is not subject to negotiation," Netanyahu said. "With an agreement or without an agreement, I am determined — we are all determined — to do whatever is necessary to ensure our security and our future."

NETANYAHU'S ISRAEL GRAPPLES WITH TRUMP-IRAN DEAL AS DETAILS REMAIN UNCLEAR

The exchange came as nuclear experts urged Trump to keep Iran’s nuclear program at the center of negotiations, warning that Tehran could use the Hormuz crisis to secure sanctions relief and other concessions before addressing its remaining nuclear capabilities.

Trump told "Fox News at Night" on Tuesday that military force remained an option if Iran abandoned the talks, while insisting Tehran could not be allowed to obtain a nuclear weapon.

"If they back out again, they’re going to get hit really hard," Trump told Fox News’ Trace Gallagher. "They know that. They understand that. I have no choice. They can’t have a nuclear weapon. It’s very simple."

"The hard hit is yet to come, and hopefully we won’t have to use it," he added.

Trump said negotiators held an "all-day negotiation" Tuesday and described the discussions as "very good." He has said the talks would initially focus on reopening the Strait of Hormuz before turning to Tehran’s nuclear program.

TRUMP WARNS IRAN WILL BE HIT 'REALLY HARD' IF NUCLEAR NEGOTIATIONS COLLAPSE AGAIN

Andrea Stricker, deputy director of the Foundation for Defense of Democracies’ Nonproliferation and Biodefense Program, said that sequence could play directly into Iran’s strategy.

"It is in the Iranians’ interest to steer the negotiations toward the issues that they most care about," Stricker told Fox News Digital, including securing major US concessions over Hormuz and "maintaining control of that crucial waterway that has proven a lifeline for Tehran to survive this war."

She said Iran would also seek oil sanctions relief, and potentially relief from all U.S. sanctions, before addressing the nuclear file.

"If Tehran is able to structure the talks that way, and I’m concerned that Trump appears to be going along with that approach, there may be little left in terms of leverage to get big concessions from the Iranians on the nuclear file down the line," Stricker said.

There is evidence that Tehran has sought to sequence the talks in its favor. Axios reported in April that Iran proposed reopening the Strait of Hormuz and ending the war before beginning nuclear negotiations, potentially reducing U.S. leverage over enrichment and Iran’s enriched-uranium stockpile.

The Washington Post later reported that Tehran was focused on preserving its leverage over Hormuz rather than engaging deeply on major nuclear restrictions.

Kelsey Davenport, director for nonproliferation policy at the Arms Control Association, agreed Iran is seeking to capitalize on the leverage it gained by disrupting maritime traffic through the Strait of Hormuz.

"The current focus on the Straits of Hormuz is not surprising. Iran is looking to capitalize on leverage gained by disrupting maritime traffic through the waterway and test if Trump is willing to negotiate in good faith," Davenport told Fox News Digital.

TRUMP WARNS IRAN FIGHTING ISN'T OVER AS HE VOWS US WILL 'WIN' AS TALKS FADE

She said Tehran understands that any durable agreement will ultimately have to address its nuclear program, but said that "At the end of this conflict, Iran will still possess the capabilities necessary to build a bomb," Davenport said, "The relevant knowledge and nuclear expertise cannot be bombed away."

"Tehran retains key materials and technologies necessary to build a bomb," she added. "If left unchecked, the nuclear program will be a source of instability and renewed conflict, even if Iran does not resume more proliferation-sensitive nuclear activities."

A proposed agreement between Iran and Oman could give Tehran some control over ships entering the Persian Gulf through the Strait of Hormuz, a senior Iranian source and two regional officials told Reuters Wednesday. One regional source described the arrangement as a concession that had already been made, although the precise meaning of Iranian "control" remained under negotiation.

Iran is also seeking fees from ships traveling through the waterway, according to Reuters, while Washington has opposed both Iranian control and mandatory transit charges.

Stricker said postponing the nuclear issues would allow the regime to preserve its remaining enriched-uranium stockpiles and avoid fully dismantling its nuclear infrastructure.

She said Iran also wants to avoid accounting for its past nuclear weapons-related work or committing to end uranium enrichment and plutonium reprocessing.

"Leaving them as a last-order issue in the negotiations likely means that we will not see the Iranians make big concessions and make a solid nuclear deal," Stricker said.

Davenport said the administration should prioritize restoring access for inspectors from the International Atomic Energy Agency before beginning detailed nuclear negotiations.

"The IAEA has not visited key Iranian nuclear sites in more than a year," she said. "It remains unclear how much of Iran’s nuclear infrastructure remains and where any gaps might be in trying to account for Iran’s nuclear materials."

She said renewed inspections would give Washington a clearer picture of Iran’s remaining facilities and materials, while helping negotiators design a verification regime capable of addressing any gaps.

Davenport also recommended pairing sanctions relief with specific, verifiable Iranian steps rather than negotiating one sweeping package.

"A series of smaller deals could build confidence in the process," she said.

Stricker urged the administration to link every concession involving Hormuz, sanctions or the U.S. blockade to a measurable Iranian step on the nuclear file.

"The best approach to ensure a solid deal is to make the nuclear issues just as important as the Strait of Hormuz, removing the blockade and other top Iranian priorities," she said.

item.title: LEE CARTER: Election shocker: The winners had a slogan, the losers just had résumés
item.description: Political candidates Abdul El-Sayed, Wesley Bell, and Trump's 2016 playbook reveal why Tuesday's primary winners had a sentence and the losers had a résumé to read.
item.content:encoded:
Tuesday night, the left won. The right won. The establishment won. The insurgents won.

In other words, nobody won.

Except for the message.

100 DAYS UNTIL MIDTERMS AND DEMOCRATS ARE WINNING BECAUSE THEY ACTUALLY HAVE A MESSAGE

The political class will now perform its traditional postmortem: find the result it agrees with and declare a sweeping ideological mandate.

But voters delivered a simpler verdict:

Tell me what you are going to do for me, and please do it before I lose interest.

The real divide was not left versus right. It was memorable versus forgettable.

'SQUAD' MEMBER'S COMEBACK BID THWARTED AS ESTABLISHMENT DEMS NOTCH VICTORY AGAINST SOCIALISTS

The winners had a sentence. The losers had a résumé.

Consider Abdul El-Sayed, who defeated Rep. Haley Stevens in Michigan’s Democratic Senate primary.

His message was: "Money out of politics. Money in your pocket. Medicare for All."

Eleven words. Three beats. A villain, a benefit and a policy. In that order.

DAVID MARCUS: IN BOOMING DETROIT, VOTERS SKEPTICAL OF SOCIALISM SNAKE OIL

Politicians like to imagine voters carefully comparing policy frameworks. Voters are usually wondering why everything costs so much and whether anyone in public life has noticed.

Stevens made the respectable case: experience, credentials and electability. All of that may have been true. It was also about her.

"I can win" is not a promise to voters. It is a candidate asking the public to participate in her career planning.

A résumé is evidence. It is not a reason. No one has ever left a rally humming, "She performs well in hypothetical general-election matchups."

DEM PRIMARY ERUPTS AS ESTABLISHMENT FAVORITE DISMISSES RIVAL AS ‘CELEBRITY CANDIDATE’

The same dynamic appeared in Missouri, although ideology changed costumes.

Former Squad member Cori Bush warned that billionaires and outside interests were trying to control her district.

Her opponent Wesley Bell answered with six words: "Progressives are supposed to make progress."

It was a lethal little sentence.

EX-'SQUAD' MEMBER FIGHTS FOR COMEBACK AS SOCIALIST WING RAMPS UP WAR ON DEM ESTABLISHMENT

Bell took a word Bush believed she owned — "progressive" — and handed it back with a new definition: not posture, purity or national attention, but results.

Bush offered an enemy. Bell offered a standard.

A villain alone is not enough. It is only the first half of the argument.

The complete version is:

FOX NEWS POLL: VOTERS WANT MAJOR CHANGE AMID ECONOMIC AND POLITICAL DISCONTENT

They are doing this to you, and I will do this for you.

Too many candidates never reach the second clause. They mistake indignation for persuasion.

But anger is an accelerant, not a destination. It can start the car. It cannot tell you where you are going.

Donald Trump understood this in 2016.

China was taking the jobs; he would bring them back.

Washington had lost control of the border; he would build the wall.

America had been diminished; he would make it great again.

Villain. Action. Benefit.

FOX NEWS POLL: COOL YOUR SERVERS! VOTERS REJECT DATA CENTERS

One could object to every detail and still understand the whole thing before the elevator doors closed.

Republicans saw their own version in Michigan’s gubernatorial primary. John James spoke about restoration, work, security and a Michigan comeback. Perry Johnson emphasized a sweeping audit of state government.

An audit may be useful. But it is a process.

A comeback is a promise.

Politicians adore process words because they sound responsible. Voters hear paperwork.

They are not dreaming of an interagency working group. They would like the electric bill to go down.

This may be why data centers became one of the night’s more revealing issues.

William Lawrence made opposition to unchecked data-center development central to his Michigan campaign. He took something vast and abstract — artificial intelligence infrastructure — and brought it home.

"AI infrastructure policy" is remote.

"Your family may pay more to power someone else’s data center" can move votes.

The closer an issue gets to the kitchen table, the less ideological it feels.

That is also why affordability has become the great unifying language of recent elections.

Politicians with little else in common have discovered that voters are preoccupied with the same rude facts: rent, groceries, child care, health care and the shrinking distance between a paycheck and a minor financial emergency.

But "affordability" is not, by itself, a message. It becomes persuasive only when people can picture it: the prescription they can fill, the rent increase they avoid, the utility bill they can manage.

Voters do not experience the economy as a set of indicators. They experience it as a series of small humiliations.

The grocery cart edited at checkout. The dinner out quietly canceled. The home that now seems permanently one promotion away. The medicine postponed.

The party that speaks most clearly to that experience will have an advantage. The one that answers with macroeconomic data will deserve what happens next.

Tuesday’s results also suggest something we should not miss.

Americans can be anti-establishment and anti-mayhem at the same time.

They can want change and reassurance. A fighter and a grown-up. Someone who will break the right things and leave the rest of the house standing.

This confuses political professionals, who prefer voters to fit neatly into ideological boxes.

Voters persist in being people.

The quality that matters is not always moderation. It is translation.

Can a candidate turn an ideology into an outcome? A policy into a picture? A political argument into something people can see in their own lives?

Tuesday’s winners were not uniformly progressive, moderate, populist or establishment.

What they shared was the ability to place the voter inside the story.

Too many political appeals begin with "I."

I fought. I led. I delivered. I have a plan.

The voter is expected to applaud this autobiographical achievement and infer a benefit.

The stronger appeal begins with an understood "you."

Your money. Your town. Your family. Your future.

Every campaign should have to pass a second-person test.

Can voters hear themselves in it? Can they explain what changes if the candidate wins? Can they repeat the central idea in 10 seconds?

If not, the campaign does not have a message.

It has material.

Both parties will now produce impressive documents announcing that voters endorsed whatever the authors believed on Monday.

But voters may have said something less ideological and more useful:

Stop making us work so hard.

Do not hand us a list and call it a vision.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE FOX NEWS OPINION

Do not describe your ambition and call it our future.

Do not give us a villain and forget the rescue.

Tell us what is wrong. Tell us what you will do. Tell us how life will be different.

Then stop talking before you ruin it.

Tuesday night was not a triumph of the left or the right.

It was a triumph of the personal over the procedural, the promise over the résumé and the memorable over the merely correct.

The winners gave voters a sentence.

The losers gave them something to read.

item.title: WNBA silent on whether French transgender star dominating women's league would be eligible to play
item.description: Julie Tétart led France's LF2 in scoring and rebounding, but the WNBA and WNBPA won't say if the transgender player is eligible under the CBA.
item.content:encoded:
The WNBA and the Women’s National Basketball Players Association still have not said whether the most dominant player in a French women’s professional basketball league would be eligible to play in the WNBA.

Transgender basketball player Julie Tétart, a biological male, plays for Monaco in Ligue Féminine 2 (LF2), France’s second-tier women’s basketball league.

Tétart averaged 21 points and 20 rebounds per game during the 2025-26 season, leading LF2 in both categories.

FRENCH TRANS PHENOM JULIE TÉTART LOOKS WNBA-READY — SO WHY HASN’T THE ‘INCLUSIVE’ LEAGUE CALLED?

Eurobasket.com also named the 34-year-old its All-French LF2 Player of the Year, Defensive Player of the Year and Domestic Player of the Year.

Those numbers certainly sound WNBA-worthy.

Plus, Tétart told OutKick/Fox News Digital that playing in the WNBA is "a childhood dream" and said, "If they contact me, I won’t say no."

So, OutKick/Fox News Digital asked the WNBA and the Women’s National Basketball Players Association a simple question: Would Julie Tétart be eligible to play in the league?

Neither organization responded to the initial inquiries or a subsequent follow-up specifically addressing Tétart’s eligibility under the collective bargaining agreement.

SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM SPEAKS OUT TO PROTECT GIRLS AS WNBA ALL-STAR INITIATIVE BACKS ‘GENDER-EXPANSIVE’ GROUP

The question shouldn’t be difficult. After all, the league’s newly signed CBA appears to provide a clear eligibility standard.

Article XIII, Section 1(a) states: "Only players who are women are eligible to play in the WNBA."

Sounds simple, right?

But as OutKick/Fox News Digital previously reported, the 409-page agreement never defines "woman" or "women." The terms "transgender" and "gender identity" don’t appear anywhere in the document.

The CBA contains detailed definitions for dozens of other terms. Yet the agreement doesn’t define the word that determines who may play in the league.

That omission was already notable when Indiana Fever star Caitlin Clark said leagues and governing bodies should work with athletes to determine who should be included in women’s sports.

OutKick/Fox News Digital previously sought clarification about the standard after Clark’s comments.

At that point, the league could treat the question as theoretical.

It isn’t theoretical anymore.

Tétart gives the WNBA a concrete case: a professional player in a women’s league who led LF2 in scoring and rebounding and has publicly expressed interest in the WNBA.

Would the WNBA consider Tétart a "woman" for purposes of Article XIII?

Would eligibility be determined by biological sex, gender identity, hormone levels or some other standard?

CHERYL REEVE SENDS CLEAR MESSAGE TO SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM WITH ‘TRANS KIDS BELONG’ SHIRT DURING FEVER-LYNX GAME

The CBA doesn’t say, leaving the league’s eligibility standard unclear.

The question is separate from age, draft and international-player eligibility provisions, which the CBA addresses in detail.

The WNBA has repeatedly presented itself as an inclusive, progressive sports league. But "inclusion" doesn’t answer the basic question: What is a woman, according to the WNBA and the WNBPA?

Either Tétart is eligible or Tétart isn’t.

If Tétart is eligible, the league should explain the standard and how that standard protects fairness for female players.

If Tétart isn’t eligible, the league should identify the rule or policy that makes a biological male ineligible. The CBA’s current language doesn’t provide that clarity publicly.

This isn’t a request for the WNBA to comment on an abstract political debate. It’s a request for the league to apply its own eligibility rule to a specific professional basketball player.

The same applies to the WNBPA. The union agreed to language stating that only women may play in the league, so players deserve to know how that language would apply to a biological male currently dominating a women’s league.

A professional player has publicly expressed interest in a WNBA opportunity.

The league has a rule that supposedly determines whether that opportunity is possible.

But when asked whether Julie Tétart qualifies under that rule, the WNBA and WNBPA had nothing to say.

item.title: 49ers star Dre Greenlaw lambasts Denver's altitude after Broncos' tenure: 'Fighting demons'
item.description: Dre Greenlaw reveals how Denver's altitude, a quad strain, and Sean Payton's frustration made his Broncos tenure feel isolating before his 49ers return.
item.content:encoded:
Home is where the heart is. For linebacker Dre Greenlaw, that certainly was not with the Denver Broncos.

Greenlaw spent last season with the Broncos after signing a three-year, $31.5 million contract, but was cut almost a year later. Greenlaw then returned to the San Francisco 49ers, where he spent the first six years of his career, on a one-year deal. While it wasn’t the main reason Greenlaw left Denver, he certainly won’t miss the altitude of the Mile High City.

"F—ing altitude," Greenlaw told The Athletic. "My mouth’s dry, my nose is dry, I can’t sleep. … I’m fighting demons left and right."

"I tell you, it’s different being here in California," Greenlaw said. "This fresh air, bro, it makes a difference. You feel like you can run all day out here."

Greenlaw’s Broncos tenure got off to an inauspicious start, as he suffered a severe quadriceps strain on the second day of OTAs, and it held him out until Week 7. Greenlaw said he felt head coach Sean Payton’s ire because he wasn’t able to be on the field.

"We were good, especially when I first came in," Greenlaw said. "And then you pop your quad, people start looking at you. Then, when we played the Jaguars (on Dec. 21), I had a little bit of a hamstring (injury). After that, you kind of feel when the coach is, like, not really messing with you. I felt alone."

I should have taken it slow. (But) naturally, they’d just paid me, so that’s all I wanted to do — go show them what I could do. And it bit me in the ass, the second day I got there."

"I know what I could have done better, as far as being in that film," he said. "That’s where I feel like I let myself and everybody down."

item.title: Senate confirms new CDC director as diarrhea-causing parasite outbreak sweeps US
item.description: Dr. Erica Schwartz was confirmed as CDC director along party lines amid concerns over whether she would stand up to Robert F. Kennedy Jr. on vaccines.
item.content:encoded:
The Senate confirmed the next director of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) as viral outbreaks wreak havoc across the country, and as lawmakers worry whether they’ve found someone to stand up to President Donald Trump’s top health official.

The upper chamber confirmed Dr. Erica Schwartz to be the next CDC director on Wednesday along party lines. Her confirmation comes as a Cyclospora outbreak, commonly known as the diarrhea parasite, carves its way across the U.S. from contaminated lettuce.

Schwartz is the latest person to lead the agency during Trump’s second term in a position that has seen nearly a half dozen different names and faces helming the nation’s disease-fighting outfit.

CYCLOSPORA OUTBREAK: IS IT STILL SAFE TO EAT AT RESTAURANTS? HERE'S WHAT TO KNOW

She almost didn’t make the cut for a full confirmation vote.

Lawmakers on the Senate Health, Education, Labor and Pensions (HELP) Committee grilled Schwartz on whether she would actually stand up to the Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. and his position on vaccines.

Notably, HELP Committee Chair Bill Cassidy, R-La., who proved the decisive vote to confirm Kennedy last year, didn’t buy whether she would just take orders or make scientific and medically-based decisions.

TRUMP BLASTS SEN BILL CASSIDY AS ‘DISLOYAL DISASTER,’ PUSHES CHALLENGER JULIA LETLOW IN LOUISIANA GOP PRIMARY

When pressed during her initial committee hearing whether she would buck orders that were politically motivated, Schwartz told Cassidy, "The secretary will absolutely allow me to be CDC director."

"I feel like I’m having to go after this question a little bit more firmly than I feel like I should," Cassidy said. "You can be CDC director and just take orders. We need a CDC director that will actually stand up to crazy, stupid things being said that undermine faith in immunization."

That changed, though, and Schwartz cleared her committee test. Cassidy, who has used his newfound freedom to test the waters against the administration after being ousted by a Trump-backed opponent in his primary, said the agency "needs someone who understands that the way to prevent vaccine-preventable diseases is to reassure the public that vaccines are safe and effective."

TRUMP SURGEON GENERAL PICK SPARKS BACKLASH, SPLITS MAHA MOVEMENT

"I’m confident that she knows what she is doing and will stand against those who do not," he said.

Schwartz, who served as deputy surgeon general during Trump’s first term, is not the first CDC director to be confirmed during this Congress.

The first was Susan Monarez, who lasted only a month in the role.

Monarez received glowing praise from Trump during her confirmation process, but was swiftly booted from the position over what appeared to be a disagreement with Kennedy over vaccines.

item.title: Commanders filling wide receiver need with Stefon Diggs, leaving Brandon Aiyuk to stew in his odd behavior
item.description: The Commanders chose Stefon Diggs over Brandon Aiyuk, whose off-putting behavior has NFL teams privately expressing concerns about his locker room fit.
item.content:encoded:
The Washington Commanders, desperately wanting to add wide receiver help for their offense, had basically two obvious and productive veteran options from which to pick – Stefon Diggs or Brandon Aiyuk.

So, the guy who has played for three different teams the past three seasons and somehow wore out his welcome despite producing two 1,000-yard seasons in that time – Diggs?

Or the guy who signed a big contract with the San Francisco 49ers in 2024, got injured, didn't play in 2025, and has become a candidate for an intervention because of his bizarre behavior in recent months – Aiyuk?

STEFON DIGGS FOUND NOT GUILTY ON STRANGULATION AND ASSAULT CHARGES, NOW EYES NFL FREE AGENCY

The Commanders are going with Diggs.

Diggs is set to sign with the Commanders, NFL Network first reported on Wednesday. Diggs will agree to what is expected to be a one-year contract and it will not be a minimum salary deal.

Diggs will join a wide receiver room replete with other veterans, including Terry McLaurin, Treylon Burks, Luke McCaffery and Dyami Brown, all who must produce while rookie Antonio Williams develops.

This is good for Diggs.

He's from the DMV (D.C., Maryland, and Virginia), he's coming off his first fully healthy offseason in three years, and he's once again playing with a good quarterback in Jayden Daniels.

This is not good, however, for Aiyuk.

It's a full-on public statement of what NFL personnel people have been privately telling Fox News Digital about Aiyuk's behavior. It is filled with off-putting, perhaps even disconcerting antics, and teams don't want to add that to their locker room.

What antics, you ask?

BRANDON AIYUK'S SOCIAL MEDIA POST MOCKING KYLE SHANAHAN'S CAR CRASH DRAWS BACKLASH AND COULD COST HIM A JOB

There's more but you get the drift.

Aiyuk didn't hide his desire to go to the Commanders because he desperately wants out of San Francisco and Daniels was his college teammate at Arizona State, where the two had good chemistry.

The Commanders expressed some interest in Aiyuk with the 49ers months ago.

SIGN UP TO GET THE LATEST SPORTS NEWS

But that interested waned. And now one can only imagine how Aiyuk will react to the news that the team offering his best chance for playing this season is going in another direction.

It might serve as a lesson for him to cut back on his reputation-harming conduct.

Or not.

item.title: FAA investigating possible violation of safety protocol involving Trump, Marine One
item.description: The FAA is reviewing a loss of separation between a commercial plane departing Reagan National Airport and Marine One carrying Trump to Los Angeles.
item.content:encoded:
The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) said it is reviewing a potential violation of a new safety protocol after an incident Tuesday involving a commercial plane and the Marine One helicopter with President Donald Trump on board, Fox News Digital confirmed.

The incident occurred when a commercial plane took off from Reagan International Airport at the same time that Trump was departing the White House on Marine One, according to The Wall Street Journal.

The White House said Trump was never in any danger.

AIR TRAFFIC CONTROL AUDIO CAPTURES TENSE MOMENT TWO PLANES NEARLY COLLIDED AT BOSTON LOGAN AIRPORT

"Marine One flights are piloted by some of the best aviators in the world, and at no point was the president in harm’s way," White House spokesman Kush Desai told Fox News in a statement.

The FAA, in a statement to Fox News Digital, reiterated the White House's point about the president's safety.

"Based on our preliminary safety review, there was momentary loss of separation, after which the aircraft continued to move away from one another. The air traffic controller was in contact with both the commercial pilot and Marine One pilot during the loss of separation. As the White House has said, the president was never in danger. We are continuing to review the incident and will implement any appropriate corrective actions based on our findings," the statement said.

A loss of separation is a breach of FAA rules that stipulate that aircraft at the same height must be at least three miles apart if they are within 40 miles of an Airport Surveillance Radar (ASR) antenna.

TRUMP TAKES INAUGURAL FLIGHT ABOARD NEW AIR FORCE ONE AHEAD OF LIBRARY DEBUT HONORING FAMED OUTDOORSMAN

Trump was departing the White House for a planned trip to Los Angeles when the incident occurred.

When contacted for comment, the U.S. Secret Service referred Fox News to the White House and FAA's comments.

Fox News' Patrick Ward contributed to this post.

item.title: 5 Mexican cartel bosses charged in weapons, drug trafficking, timeshare fraud schemes, DOJ says
item.description: CJNG cartel members face federal indictments for drug trafficking, weapons charges, and a timeshare fraud scheme that stole $400M from seniors.
item.content:encoded:
The U.S. Department of Justice (DOJ), along with the heads of numerous other federal agencies, announced Wednesday indictments of members of the Jalisco New Generation Cartel (CJNG) for drug trafficking, weapons charges and for targeting elderly Americans in sprawling timeshare fraud schemes.

The revelation was part of a wider inter-agency news conference Wednesday announcing a sweeping set of enforcement actions targeting the CJNG in Mexico.

"These sophisticated organizations use violence and fear to maintain control over the importation of deadly narcotics in the United States, including fentanyl, cocaine, meth, and other illegal drugs. Their actions spread violence and death to our communities," Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche announced during the news conference.

"These cartel members have been charged with a range of crimes, including running drug networks, organizing highly trained hitmen responsible for murders and attempted assassinations, procuring weapons, money laundering and deadly drug manufacturing and distribution. Three of the alleged cartel members were also allegedly committing a sophisticated fraud targeting elderly Americans in an alleged timeshare fraud scheme," Blanche added.

'NARCO-TERRORIST' FAMILY MEMBERS TARGETED IN RUBIO'S LATEST VISA CRACKDOWN

As part of the enforcement, the DOJ's criminal division brought federal charges against five senior members of the cartel, including drug trafficking and firearms offenses, Assistant Attorney General Tysen Duva said. Duva also provided further details about the fraud scheme targeting elderly Americans.

"CJNG targeted Americans who are aspiring to own or already own timeshares in Mexico, many of them elderly, and promised them profits for selling or renting them. But first, the victims had to pay taxes and advance fees. Of course, the profits never came. Once someone paid, the fraudsters contacted them again, posing as lawyers or officials who could recover the money for another fee," Duva explained.

"Of course it was fake. The scheme morphed and continued, with the fraudsters even claiming that the victims actually paid a cartel and would be arrested if they did not pay more, which they did. One particular victim, an 83-year-old individual, an American who bought a timeshare many years ago for $179,000, was duped at each level of this phase. He paid advance fees to begin with. He fell for fake real estate websites and title companies. He was victimized again by attorneys who sent their bar information and fake websites, who claimed that they could get his money back. Of course they were impersonators and they could not," Duva continued.

FAKE BOOKING.COM TRAVEL CREDIT SCAM TARGETS TRAVELERS

item.title: Houston Texans star practices in pads for first time in nearly two years after 2024 career-threatening injury
item.description: Tank Dell practiced in full pads at Houston Texans training camp on Wednesday, his first NFL action in pads since a December 2024 knee injury.
item.content:encoded:
The snapshot of Tank Dell crumpled in that end zone and desperately pointing at his dislocated knee in December of 2024 is something to recall but not relive because it was horrible to witness.

Dell, 26, hasn't played football since that moment, raising concerns he'd never play again and amid the echoes of naysayers predicting he'd never be the same.

But Tank Dell's comeback is on. And on Wednesday that long journey took a significant step when he stepped on an NFL practice field with his teammates in full pads for the first time at Houston Texans training camp.

ONE OF NFL'S FASTEST PLAYERS HAS 'NO POWER' IN ONE INJURED LEG, CASTING DOUBTS ON 2026 SEASON

Dell worked during significant parts of practice, although he took some periods and drills off. Yes, this return that has Dell playing for the first time since 2024 is a process.

And neither he nor anyone else in the Texans' organization is ready to make bold predictions about the comeback other than stating the goal is competing in 2026.

That's understandable if you know the history

While catching a touchdown pass against the Kansas City Chiefs, Dell collided with teammate Jared Wayne, causing his left knee to buckle violently beneath him.

Doctors ultimately determined Dell dislocated his knee, tore multiple major knee ligaments, ruptured his patellar tendon, suffered significant damage to the meniscus and surrounding soft tissue, and sustained a vascular injury that required emergency surgery to restore blood flow to his lower leg.

The severity of the damage spoke for itself: Dell's career seemed on the brink.

For a receiver like Dell, whose game is built on sudden acceleration, sharp cuts, and change of direction, the challenge of returning to form is daunting. Even after doctors clear such a player to resume football activities, rebuilding confidence in the repaired knee, restoring strength and flexibility, and withstanding the physical demands of NFL competition can take years – if it happens at all.

Dell has made steady progress through his rehabilitation, but his recovery has been viewed as one of the league's most difficult injury comebacks because of the extraordinary extent of the damage.

"It’s been a roller coaster ride, to say the least," Dell said when he spoke to reporters in June. "It’s been a long journey, but I’m built for it, and I’m ready for it, and I was ready for it.

"I’m getting through it, and it’s light at the end of the tunnel, so I’m almost there."

Not quite.

Dell's ramp-up to a game is not one step or even one week away. The Texans have been deliberate in ordering his return and the next step is seeing how he reacts to Wednesday's practice – checking whether there's pain, swelling, discomfort.

If Dell clears that hurdle, then he'll practice again. And again. And again.

SIGN UP TO GET THE LATEST SPORTS NEWS

Eventually, barring a setback, Dell might get snaps in a preseason game. Then, if he clears that, the regular-season beckons.

The Texans open the regular season on Sept. 13 against the Buffalo Bills at home against the Buffalo Bills. That's seemingly a long way away.

But Tank Dell got one significant step closer on Wednesday.

item.title: Dem drops US Senate bid, leaving independent candidate as lone challenger to incumbent GOP Sen Mike Rounds
item.description: Democratic Senate candidate Julian Beaudion dropped out of the South Dakota race, leaving only GOP Sen. Mike Rounds and independent challenger Brian Bengs in the contest.
item.content:encoded:
Julian Beaudion, the Democratic candidate who was challenging Republican Sen. Mike Rounds of South Dakota, announced he is dropping his election bid, a move that leaves independent candidate Brian Bengs going head-to-head against the incumbent lawmaker.

"As many of you know, we experienced a devastating house fire while continuing to navigate significant personal financial hardship," Beaudion explained in part of a lengthy statement issued Tuesday. Today, my first responsibility is to them.

"After the fire, an opponent and those associated with the opponent, hit my family and I with intimidating threats to drop out of this race,' he said in the statement.

"Those attacks were personal and never about politics. The mental and physical safety of my family is my priority and for this reason alone, I step aside. This is a time for my family to heal and for South Dakota voters to choose a Senator. Not a time for me to talk of specific threats and attacks. But rest assured that time will come."

GOP GOVERNOR SURVIVES CHALLENGE FROM BITCOIN EVANGELIST IN GUBERNATORIAL RUNOFF

Beaudion said he will not back either of the remaining candidates in the contest.

"Let me be clear, I will not be endorsing or supporting Brian Bengs in this race," he noted. "Likewise, I cannot support Senator Mike Rounds."

TRUMP ENDORSES GOP SENATOR YEARS AFTER ASSERTING 'I WILL NEVER ENDORSE THIS JERK AGAIN'

Bengs, who ran for U.S. Senate as a Democrat in 2022 but lost to GOP Sen. Now South Dakotans who want to vote against Washington's cost-raising agenda and corruption can come together regardless of party. Let’s look forward to November and retiring Big Money Mike Rounds."

South Dakota Democratic Party Chair Shane Merrill said in a statement, "Julian would have made an outstanding U.S. Senator for South Dakota."

REPUBLICAN WHO REPORTEDLY DROPPED OUT DEFEATS TRUMP'S PICK IN KEY SWING-DISTRICT PRIMARY

Thank you Julian for your dedication to the people of South Dakota," Merrill noted.

item.title: El-Sayed campaign backed by over $100,000 from dozens of members of group with alleged terror ties
item.description: Abdul El-Sayed's Senate campaign collected over $115,000 from CAIR officials and leaders, including an executive who praised Hamas on Oct. 7.
item.content:encoded:
FIRST ON FOX: GRAND RAPIDS, MI - Michigan Democratic Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed's campaign has collected more than $115,000 from individuals who work for or have held leadership roles with the Council on American-Islamic Relations (CAIR), which has been designated a terrorist organization by the United Arab Emirates and formally designated or labeled as such in Florida and Texas.

A Fox News Digital review found that El-Sayed, who has made getting "money out of politics" a central campaign rallying cry, has accepted donations from at least 41 individuals who either work for CAIR, formerly worked for CAIR, or have served in leadership positions with the organization.

The donor list includes several of CAIR's highest-ranking officials, including national Board Chair Manal Fakhoury, national Board Treasurer Eyas Abdeen, national Vice Chair Emad Sabbah, and CAIR-Michigan board member Jukaku Tayeb, El-Sayed's father-in-law.

Tayeb has been one of the largest financial backers of the super PAC supporting El-Sayed's campaign and is also part of the founding committee of the Islamic Society of North America (ISNA), a group linked to Hamas and Muslim Brotherhood funding, Washington Free Beacon first reported.

DEMS CLASH OVER AIPAC MONEY, ‘OGRE’ ATTACK AND ELECTABILITY DURING CRUCIAL SENATE DEBATE

One donor, CAIR Executive Director Nihad Awad, listed in FEC records under the name Nehad Hammad, drew national condemnation after saying he was "happy" to see Hamas break out of Gaza on Oct. 7, 2023, and arguing Israel "does not have the right to self-defense" as an occupying power.

The contributions were not limited to Michigan. Fox News Digital identified donations from CAIR national leaders and officials affiliated with chapters in California, Arizona, Texas, Georgia, Washington, Illinois, Minnesota and Ohio, among other states, illustrating the breadth of support El-Sayed received from within the organization's leadership ranks.

Other names on the donor list include CAIR-California Governance Board Treasurer Rubina Alvi, CAIR-California Governance Board Chair Asaad Traina, CAIR-Michigan board member Muzammil Ahmed, who contributed $11,600 to El-Sayed's campaign, CAIR-California Governance Board member Atef Ibrahim, CAIR-California Governance Board member Dina Ezzeddine, and former CAIR National Board Chair Roula Allouch.

EL-SAYED PALS AROUND WITH FAR-LEFT STREAMER HASAN PIKER THE DAY BEFORE CRUCIAL MICHIGAN SENATE ELECTION

El-Sayed has maintained ties to CAIR beyond campaign fundraising. In 2022, he appeared at a CAIR event and was paid for a speaking engagement, where he criticized Oklahoma's ban on Sharia law and compared it to the Trail of Tears, Washington Free Beacon reported.

CAIR has long been the subject of controversy over its alleged ties to Hamas. In 2007, federal prosecutors named the organization an unindicted co-conspirator in the Holy Land Foundation terrorism financing case, the largest terrorism financing prosecution in U.S. history.

Although CAIR was never charged with a crime, federal prosecutors argued the organization was part of a network created to support Hamas in the United States. CAIR has denied the allegations and has challenged its inclusion as an unindicted co-conspirator.

In recent years, Florida and Texas have formally designated or labeled CAIR a terrorist organization, while the United Arab Emirates designated the group a terrorist organization in 2014 which is widely understood to stem from the UAE's view that CAIR has ties to the Muslim Brotherhood.

In response to Fox News Digital's request for comment, CAIR denied allegations that it has ties to terrorism, citing its "Dispelling Rumors About CAIR" webpage, a memorandum stating it has "repeatedly condemned antisemitism throughout our 30 years of existence" and "for decades" condemned terrorist attacks by Hamas and other designated terrorist groups, as well as a 2009 statement saying, "We unequivocally condemn all acts of terrorism, whether carried out by al-Qa’ida, the Real IRA, FARC, Hamas, ETA, or any other group designated by the U.S. Department of State as a ‘Foreign Terrorist Organization."

CAIR also cited a National Board statement condemning antisemitism and the Oct. 7, 2023, attacks, and a 2023 editorial in which National Executive Director Nihad Awad said he agreed with the organization's condemnation of attacks on civilians.

Fox News Digital reached out to the El-Sayed campaign for comment.

El-Sayed has repeatedly drawn criticism from Republicans and pro-Israel advocates over his associations and comments related to the Middle East, including campaigning with far-left streamer Hasan Piker, his response to an attack targeting a Detroit synagogue, and declining to comment on the death of Iran's supreme leader, citing constituents in Dearborn who were mourning.

El-Sayed defeated Dem. Rep. Haley Stevens in the Democratic Senate primary on Tuesday night in a race that was much closer than most pundits expected. El-Sayed will face off against Republican Mike Rogers, a former congressman, in November.

item.title: Schumer claims victory as Senate moves to avert shutdown; GOP says he got played
item.description: The Senate advanced a continuing resolution unanimously, but Republicans and Democrats clashed over whether the deal blocks Trump's federal grants rule.
item.content:encoded:
The Senate quietly moved its solution to halt a government shutdown through another key step as the tenuous truce between Republicans and Democrats continues to hold.

In the midst of a hectic, albeit open-ended and uncertainty-laden schedule, the upper chamber advanced its continuing resolution (CR) unanimously on Wednesday. 

While not the final vote, it’s a strong sign that neither side wants to thrust the federal government into uncertainty as the midterms near.

It marks a sharp departure from the shutdown politics of the last year and follows Senate Republicans' hand-wringing for months that Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer, D-N.Y., would once again lead his caucus to the brink and shut the government down for political gain.

DEMOCRATS BLINK AS SCHUMER HELPS GOP CLEAR KEY SHUTDOWN HURDLE

For now, that’s not happening.

And Schumer is saying that Democrats have wanted to keep the lights on in a bipartisan manner all along.

He contended that the CR, negotiated between the top Republican and Democrat on the Senate Appropriations Committee, was a major victory for Democrats, particularly for its design to "stave off Trump's disgraceful effort to withhold federal grants from vital projects."

"I mean, what kind of country is this? You have two identical projects, one in a red state and one in a blue state funded the same way, same clean record," Schumer said. "He cancels the blue state one and says the red state one is OK."

TRUMP ADMIN PAUSING OVER $1B IN MEDICAID PAYMENTS TO MINNESOTA, CALIFORNIA OVER FRAUD, COMPLIANCE CONCERNS

The Office of Management and Budget (OMB) and the Trump administration are pushing for more control over federal grants, which critics like Schumer and others warn could be used as a political cudgel to dictate which states do and don’t get a flow of federal dollars.

If the CR passes and is signed by Trump, it will pause that rule change until Dec. 11, when the stopgap expires.

But Republicans say it’s not quite the victory Schumer thinks it is.

BOMB-THROWER DEM MAKES SHOCKING PROMISE TO KICK SCHUMER TO CURB DURING SENATE DEBATE

Sen. John Kennedy, R-La., countered that Schumer may think he won with the deal, but, in reality, it just delayed the inevitable for the White House’s plans for grant-funded projects.

"I think he's going to go back to his base and say, ‘I got the OMB rule killed,’" Kennedy said. "Well, he didn’t. I mean, I've talked to [OMB Director] Russ Vought, and the president this morning about that, and the rule can be ready by Dec. 11. So, no harm, no foul."

item.title: Hasan Piker unloads on 'Islamophobic pieces of s---' Democrats as El-Sayed faces party unity test

DEM PRIMARY ERUPTS AS ESTABLISHMENT FAVORITE DISMISSES RIVAL AS ‘CELEBRITY CANDIDATE’

EL-SAYED PALS AROUND WITH FAR-LEFT STREAMER HASAN PIKER THE DAY BEFORE CRUCIAL MICHIGAN SENATE ELECTION

"Groups and the NGOs and the consultants that have worked extensively for pro-Israel candidates to shut the f--- up about El-Sayed being a terrorist for a long enough timeline so that you know we can consolidate the base and defeat the f---ing Republican."

Moms Demand Action founder Shannon Watts highlighted Piker’s message to Democrats who supported Stevens or another primary candidate.

"Hasan Piker’s message to Dems who didn’t vote for El-Sayed: ‘You are all unbelievably Islamophobic pieces of s---,’" Watts said on X.

Rob Flaherty, ex-White House digital strategy director for former President Joe Biden, urged El-Sayed to disregard Piker as the nominee pivoted toward the general election.

REPUBLICANS GET THE DEMOCRAT THEY WANTED AS SOCIALIST ABDUL EL-SAYED WINS MICHIGAN SENATE PRIMARY

"I am not a Hasan-doomer, and I think he has an important place in the ecosystem, but I hope he and the pool party crowd head back to LA and let Abdul ignore this very bad advice," Flaherty said.

Conservative commentator Guy Benson characterized Piker as a leading surrogate addressing Democratic voters.

"Dems’ top surrogate to many Dem voters: ‘You are all unbelievably Islamophobic pieces of s---,’" Benson said.

El-Sayed repeatedly campaigned with Piker, including at college campus rallies and a Detroit pool party Monday for content creators supporting his campaign. Stevens urged El-Sayed to distance himself from the streamer, whose previous remarks about the Sept. 11 attacks, Hamas and Mao Zedong have drawn criticism.

The Associated Press declared El-Sayed the winner Wednesday after he narrowly defeated Stevens in a contest that attracted more than $80 million in spending. He will face Rogers for the seat being vacated by retiring Democratic Sen. Gary Peters.

item.title: Bigfoot hunter suggests there's a conspiracy after Cornell University denies conducting DNA tests on remains
item.description: Cornell University denies conducting a DNA test on alleged Bigfoot remains found in the Adirondack Mountains, contradicting Snake the Bigfoot Hunter.
item.content:encoded:
I hope you're sitting down for this one. The claims that a DNA test was conducted on the supposed remains of a Bigfoot by Cornell's Veterinary DNA Lab have been called into question.

This has taken a turn from finally having the answers we've all been looking for, — that the cryptid was a Neanderthal-human hybrid, as claimed by Charles Stuart, aka Snake the Bigfoot Hunter — to being back at the starting block.

That's because Cornell University denies conducting any such test for Snake. A spokesperson told the NY Post, "Cornell did not conduct any testing for [Stuart,] or present a report."

WITNESS RECOUNTS FOURTH OF JULY WEEKEND BIGFOOT SIGHTING IN CONNECTICUT, SAYS 'THERE WERE NO BOOBS'

The documents that are being pointed to as evidence that are purported to be from the university aren't from the Ivy League school, the spokesperson confirmed.

Snake the Bigfoot Hunter, who has been called a hoaxer and scammer by others in the Bigfoot community, claims to have found the body in the Adirondack Mountains in October 2024.

He's put it on display, nicknamed it Dack, and, despite Cornell's denial, claims to have had it DNA tested. The results of which determined, according to him, that "the body has 58.5% Neanderthal and 41.5% human DNA."

The reason that the university is denying that they tested the Bigfoot remains is part of a conspiracy to keep the truth from coming out, Snake suggests.

"CORNELL IS FLAT OUT LYING — I WILL NOT BE SILENCED," he fired back at The Post when they reached out to him about it.

TWO LADIES, A DOG, A LIGHTHOUSE AND A POSSIBLE BIGFOOT ENCOUNTER ON A BEACH IN MICHIGAN

"This isn't a dispute over the facts of the report — it's panic over control. I bypassed the machine and went straight to the public. I was warned from day one not to share this report. I released the unredacted DNA report anyway because I believe in transparency and the intelligence of the public."

This isn't over according to Snake the Bigfoot Hunter. He told The Post that he's planning to release a documentary that will feature a Cornell lab technician whistleblower.

The whole conspiracy against Bigfoot is going to be revealed by the person who performed the test on the remains. Snake added, "This is essentially a David VS Goliath story and we all know who wins in the end."

Until then, you can visit The Great New York State Fair at the end of August to see the supposed Bigfoot remains for yourself. Dack will be on display again this year as he was last year.

Is it real or a hoax? Is there a conspiracy to cover up the truth? Or is Snake the Bigfoot Hunter the hoaxer and scammer others claim he is and is this all about getting people out to a state fair?

Let me know what you think at sean.joseph@outkick.com.

item.title: Bernie Sanders tells James Carville to start his own party as moderate Dems warn against 'embracing extremism'
item.description: Bernie Sanders told James Carville to start his own party after the strategist vowed he wouldn't share one with Hasan Piker, who once said America deserved 9/11.
item.content:encoded:
Sen. Bernie Sanders, I-Vt., stood by far-left streamer Hasan Piker on Tuesday when pressed about a Democratic Party that included both someone like Piker and Democratic strategist James Carville, as moderate Democrats told Fox News Digital the party must abandon extremism. 

"So when someone like James Carville says he doesn't want to be in the same political party as Hasan Piker, which one are you going to take?" CNN's Abby Phillip asked Sanders Tuesday night.

"Well, that's not much of a choice," Sanders said. "If Mr. Carville doesn't want to be in my party, the party that I belong to, that Piker, that El-Sayed belongs to, he can start his own party." 

Sanders discussed the Michigan Senate race, where he endorsed Democratic candidate Abdul El-Sayed, who campaigned alongside Piker. El-Sayed narrowly defeated moderate Rep. Haley Stevens in the high-stakes Democratic Senate primary after the state finished counting votes on Wednesday, providing a boost for the party's left wing in its ideological battle with the center-left establishment.

HASAN PIKER, ABDUL EL-SAYED MOCK JAMES CARVILLE THREATENING TO LEAVE DEMOCRATS AND 'SWEETENING THE DEAL'

El-Sayed has campaigned with Piker and appeared on the far-left streamer's YouTube channel. 

The progressive senator argued that he could turn the tables and ask if people wanted to be part of a party that accepts AIPAC money or supports an "extremist" government in Israel under Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

"Do you want to be in a party which has not stood up to the AI industry because they got a lot of money from AI or from crypto?" he said. "So you can pick, you know, you can pick whatever you want to pick. But I think we need a big tent, and I think people like Piker should be welcomed into that, certainly."

Carville did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment.

Center-left think tank Third Way told Fox News Digital, "Democrats lost power in part because we lost the battle of reasonableness against Donald Trump. Voters in battleground states said in Third Way's post-election poll from the 2024 race that they saw the Democratic Party as more extreme than Republicans, 44% to 41%."

"Embracing extremism will only serve to hand Republicans a key pickup opportunity and imperil Democrats elsewhere," the group warned.

HASAN PIKER'S DEFENSE OF HAMAS HAVING 'RIGHT TO RESIST MILITARILY' DRAWS CONDEMNATION FROM HUMAN RIGHTS GROUPS

Sanders was also asked if he was comfortable with Piker saying that "America deserved 9/11" during a stream in 2019. 

"I think that's a dumb statement," Sanders said. "On the other hand, he has a whole lot of followers and a lot of things that he's saying that are making sense to a lot of people. I think, you know, we have to get above cancel culture. You know, when you're doing radio, whatever they do, podcasts three hours a day, you say dumb things."

"I suspect if you go back over your career, there may be one or two things that you've said that you may have regretted," the senator told Phillip. "But I think what we have got to do is look at the totality of where people are coming from and go forward."

After receiving widespread backlash at the time, Piker later said in an interview that he "obviously" did not mean America deserved the attacks and defended the viral quote as a critique of U.S. foreign policy.

Third Way told Fox News Digital, "Republicans are salivating at the opportunity to pummel swing voters with ads of El-Sayed embracing extremist stances. Videos of El-Sayed with his arms around Hasan Piker alongside anti-American and misogynistic quotes, like claiming America "deserved" 9/11, tweets about defunding the police, and photos of El-Sayed calling to abolish ICE will fill the timelines of voters in the middle."

"Democratic candidates like El-Sayed need to win over 60% of moderate voters to take back power and put a check on Donald Trump," the group added. "That’s not spin — that’s math. So El-Sayed has work to do as he turns to the general election and it starts with dropping the extremism." 

JAMES CARVILLE WORRIES ABOUT THE 'END OF THE TWO-PARTY SYSTEM' AS DEMOCRATIC SOCIALISTS GAIN POPULARITY

Carville told Fox News on Sunday's "The Briefing" that he would not be in the same party as Piker.

"I am not going to be in the same party with Hasan Piker," he said. "If he becomes a force in a Democratic Party, I'm out of here. I have no intention of ever being in the same political party with that guy."

Carville predicted that one of them was going to leave the party.

"I can't sit here and tell you for certain how this is going to turn out, but the one thing I can tell you for certain, Hasan Piker and James Carville are not going to be in the same political party," he said. "One of us is going to leave. It might even be me."

item.title: Tlaib moves to block ICE airport arrests, says TSA helping target immigrants
item.description: Rashida Tlaib's bill would block ICE and Border Patrol from accessing TSA passenger screening data, travel records and data broker information.
item.content:encoded:
Progressive Democrats are taking their war against President Donald Trump's handling of Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) to the skies with a new effort led by far-left Rep. Rashida Tlaib, D-Mich.

Tlaib introduced a bill on Tuesday aimed at blocking ICE and Border Patrol agents from accessing air travelers' data called the No TSA Data for ICE Act, which would curb federal immigration officials' ability to arrest noncitizens at U.S. airports.

The legislation would stop ICE and Customs and Border Protection (CBP) from being able to use data gathered by the Transportation Security Administration (TSA), which includes passenger screening records, travel records and personally identifiable passenger information purchased from private data brokers.

A TSA spokesperson ripped into Tlaib in response and argued the bill would make the U.S. vulnerable to terror threats. "As we approach the 25th anniversary of the horrific terror attacks of 9/11, it’s not shocking that some in the Democrat Party would want to neuter the Department of Homeland Security’s ability to protect Americans from terrorists," the spokesperson said.

DEMOCRAT COMPARES ICE TO 'DOMESTIC TERRORISTS' AS 111 HOUSE DEMS DEMAND TEXAS DETENTION CENTER CLOSE

"DHS was established to prevent information silos that could create blind spots against threats. Does Rep. Tlaib want our enemies to be empowered to attack the U.S. again?" the TSA spokesperson said.

The bill would also block the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) from barring an individual from trusted traveler programs like TSA PreCheck based on their First Amendment-protected activity, like attending protests or speaking out against the administration.

Tlaib's bill has little chance of getting a vote in the current Republican-controlled Congress.

If enacted, it could significantly curb the ability of DHS' separate entities to coordinate immigration enforcement.

The Michigan Democrat said in a statement that the TSA was "complicit in ICE expanding its chaos and cruelty to target our communities in our airports."

HARRIS CALLS FOR ICE PROBE AFTER MAINE SHOOTING AMID RENEWED 'BORDER CZAR' CRITICISM

"Through an information-sharing agreement signed in 2025, TSA is readily offering up our immigrant residents to suffer at the hands of ICE agents so they can fulfill their daily arrest quota. One source from ICE even said it makes for ‘easy targets’ at airports—a disgusting exploitation of immigrants in status limbo," Tlaib said. "Immigrants should be able to safely fly in this country without the fear of arrest or deportation."

Democrats have near-universally hammered the Trump administration's immigration crackdown since the president came back to the White House in January 2025.

The criticism fueled the longest partial government shutdown in history, with DHS going unfunded for 76 days as Democrats protested federal immigration agents' killing of two U.S. citizens earlier this year — which also drew ire from Republicans.

FIRST ON FOX: After her 18-year-old daughter, Hailey King, was run over by an illegal immigrant driving a truck 36 mph above the speed limit, Angel Mom Kathy Hall promised her dying daughter she was "never going to stop fighting for justice for her."

In an interview obtained exclusively by Fox News Digital from advocacy group The American Border Story, Hall recounted her daughter’s grisly killing, which, she said, launched her crusade to make sure that no other parents and children undergo the same fate.

While riding a scooter with a friend in Fayetteville, Arkansas, King was hit from behind by a speeding truck driven by illegal alien Sergio Rodriguez. According to Hall, her daughter was on her way home for dinner. Upon impact, King was thrown onto the hood of the truck. Hall said Rodriguez continued driving, swerving into another lane and sending King headfirst onto the street. King suffered a brain stem hemorrhage, inner and outer cranial hemorrhages, a burst spleen and a lacerated liver. She died shortly after the Nov. 7, 2016, incident, leaving behind her 2-year-old daughter, Brooklyn.

Hall said Rodriguez was sentenced to 17 years in prison for manslaughter, battery and leaving the scene of a crime. After just one and a half years, Hall said she was notified that Rodriguez had become eligible for parole, forcing her to repeatedly relive her trauma each time she goes to court to testify against his release.

EXCLUSIVE: DHS HONORS ANGEL FAMILIES DURING NATIONAL CRIME VICTIMS WEEK, CALLS CRIMES 'COMPLETELY PREVENTABLE'

Hall said that authorities showed up at her door the night of the incident and told her, "You need to come with us to the hospital."

She said they took her to her daughter’s hospital room where she found her "sitting up at a kind of an angle and her eyes were wide open. But she was like staring off into space."

"I knew right when I looked at her that she was gone," said Hall. "So, I sat down with her and talked to her and told her how much I love her. Told her I was never going to stop fighting for justice for her… and then her heart stopped."

Besides King, Hall said that her daughter’s friend, Osmin "David" Gutierrez, was "trapped underneath the truck for over a mile" as the illegal immigrant continued driving. She said that "when sparks started happening, [Rodriguez] pulled into an apartment complex. And when he did, David's torso was – his legs detached, [and he] was left in the driveway screaming for his life."

Gutierrez died two years later from a blood clot resulting from his lost legs.

FAMILY SHATTERED AFTER 3-TIME DEPORTED ILLEGAL IMMIGRANT ALLEGEDLY BLEW THROUGH STOP SIGN, ROILING HOUSE RACE

Despite her promise, Hall said getting justice for her daughter has been a "hard long road." After the incident, Hall said Rodriguez "disappeared for three days" before police found him. When he was apprehended, Hall said Rodriguez was released on bond in less than an hour.

She believes that Rodriguez was "protected every step of the way" during the trial process while she and her family "were treated like we were the criminals when we'd go into court."

Despite his immigration status, Hall said a decision was made not to notify U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement. She said she was told that "if we would have informed ICE that he was here and he was illegal, that they would have just picked him up and taken him down to Texas and sent him back and he would have never had to deal with the death of [her] daughter."

At the time, Hall said the family felt this "was kind of putting us in a rock and a hard place."

"It's so confusing to be there and say, ‘OK, do I want him to be deported right now or do I just want him to spend time either way and get him out?’" she said. "We had no idea, you know, a choice like that. What kind of decision do you make?"

'SLAP ON THE WRIST': ILLEGAL IMMIGRANT TRUCKER'S SENTENCE IGNITES OUTRAGE AFTER CRASH KILLED 3

item.title: Barry Manilow cancels concert 45 minutes before start amid ongoing lung cancer recovery
item.description: Barry Manilow canceled his Lexington show just 45 minutes before showtime, citing unforeseen circumstances amid his ongoing lung cancer battle.
item.content:encoded:
Barry Manilow canceled his Kentucky show on Tuesday just 45 minutes before it was scheduled to start.

"Due to unforeseen circumstances tonight’s show in Lexington has been rescheduled," Manilow, who was diagnosed with lung cancer last year, wrote on X ahead of the concert. No other explanation was given.

BARRY MANILOW, 82, GIVES UPDATE ON HIS CANCER BATTLE AS HE CANCELS MORE TOUR DATES

"Sending hugs x take care and remember you must come first," one user wrote on X.

"I'm so sorry you've had to reschedule tonight's show," another added. "Please look after yourself Barry, sending much love and healing energy from across the pond."

In December, Manilow revealed he had been diagnosed with early-stage lung cancer after doctors discovered a cancerous spot on his left lung following a bout of bronchitis.

"As many of you know I recently went through six weeks of bronchitis followed by a relapse of another five weeks," Manilow wrote on Instagram at the time. "Even though I was over the bronchitis and back on stage at the Westgate Las Vegas, my wonderful doctor ordered an MRI just to make sure that everything was OK. The MRI discovered a cancerous spot on my left lung that needs to be removed. It's pure luck (and a great doctor) that it was found so early. That's the good news."

"The bad news is that now that the Christmas A Gift of Love concerts are over I'm going into surgery to have the spot removed," he continued. "The doctors do not believe it has spread and I'm taking tests to confirm the diagnosis. So, that's it. No chemo. No radiation. Just chicken soup and I Love Lucy reruns."

In February, Manilow announced he was rescheduling additional February and March dates on the tour after a "very depressing visit" with his surgeon.

item.title: DAVID MARCUS: Experts crowned El-Sayed — then Michigan voters turned his win into a near-disaster
item.description: Polls gave Abdul El-Sayed double-digit leads, but Haley Stevens nearly pulled off a stunning upset in Michigan's Democratic Senate primary race.
item.content:encoded:
Over the past week, prior to far-left candidate Abdul El-Sayed squeaking to a possible victory over Rep. Haley Stevens in Tuesday’s Democratic Senate primary, the contest was treated by almost everyone in the news media as over, with El-Sayed a shoo-in.

I had been in Michigan reporting on the race, and what I wrote was the exact opposite: It was clear to me the race was tightening, especially after the endorsement of Gov. Gretchen Whitmer. So when I saw every subsequent poll giving El-Sayed double-digit leads, I was shocked and a bit nervous.

Maybe, for the first time, the ground had lied to me and the numbers guys had this one right. But once again, the ground coverage defeated the aerial polling.

DEM PRIMARY ERUPTS AS ESTABLISHMENT FAVORITE DISMISSES RIVAL AS ‘CELEBRITY CANDIDATE’

But by Wednesday morning, this race, in which El-Sayed held a 95% to 5% advantage in prediction markets, had not been called, with El-Sayed seeming to head toward a meager 1- to 3-point victory, with his total under 50%.

Notably, Michigan state Sen. Mallory McMorrow, who dropped out of the race, still netted 4% — or, put another way, the difference.

As for the polling, the last five public polls had El-Sayed winning by 19, 17, 14, 16 and 11 points, respectively. The news media took this as gospel, and instead of covering a surging Stevens with a real chance to win — as I did — they covered an El-Sayed coronation pre-party.

What surprised me so much about this polling was that in Detroit, after dozens of interviews, I couldn’t find anyone voting for El-Sayed who wasn’t already an activist in some way. The more ordinary the politics or occupation of the voter, the more likely that person was to support Stevens.

DAVID MARCUS: IN BOOMING DETROIT, VOTERS SKEPTICAL OF SOCIALISM SNAKE OIL

As I put it in these pages then, "Many Democratic voters I talked to wanted a steadier hand on the system, and they want to beat Trump and the GOP. But they don’t want to blow up the system."

Those voters, whom I met in Detroit diners and bars, were invisible to the pollsters. Yet, in the end, between Stevens and McMorrow, they were the majority of Democratic voters.

There needs to be a serious reckoning over how journalists use polls and prediction markets in the wake of this historic polling miss, because there is every reason to believe Stevens could have won if her very real momentum had been accurately described.

Elections are stories, and they have arcs. The last week of this campaign, by all rights, should have been about "The Stevens Comeback," but instead, the polls told the story: "El-Sayed Blowout."

DSA MEMBER LEADS DEM PRIMARY IN MIDWEST BATTLEGROUND BUT TRAILS LIKELY GOP NOMINEE: POLL

How many potential Stevens voters stayed home on Tuesday as a result? We will never know.

The national coverage throughout the week leading to Election Day was that even with Whitmer’s endorsement and that of Rep. James Clyburn, D-S.C., to shore up the Black vote, El-Sayed and his communist-aligned podcaster ally, Hasan Piker, were cruising to victory.

Let’s be honest: It is the story everybody wanted. It is the sexy story of young socialists upending the Democratic Party establishment, but the embellished polls may well have become a self-fulfilling prophecy.

For Republican Senate nominee Mike Rogers, this is all excellent news. He wanted to run against the socialist-aligned El-Sayed, and now he will. He also has the advantage of El-Sayed’s being wounded by what turned into a humiliating underperformance.

EL-SAYED PALS AROUND WITH FAR-LEFT STREAMER HASAN PIKER THE DAY BEFORE CRUCIAL MICHIGAN SENATE ELECTION

Rogers should also be buoyed by El-Sayed surrogate Piker’s statement Tuesday night about possibly reaching out to Stevens voters. Piker said: saying, "Everyone being like, 'Abdul has a f--- ton of work to do mending bridges'… You are all unbelievably Islamophobic pieces of s---. You literally called the dude a f---ing terrorist for months on end…  And now you're going to say sit there and be like, 'you really gotta come to me now.'"

CLICK HERE FOR MORE FOX NEWS OPINION

These are not the sweet, sonorous sounds of intraparty unity.

The race between Rogers and El-Sayed will be close and hard-fought, and I will find my way back to the Great Lakes State to take the temperature. In the meantime, the news media must be much more skeptical of polling because it may have turned this primary.

item.title: Controversial socialist chef flip-flops on abolish the police, says she’s ‘serious about public safety’
item.description: Francesca Hong now says she is "serious about public safety" after previously calling to defund and abolish the police in her 2020 tweets.
item.content:encoded:
Controversial chef and democratic socialist candidate Francesca Hong has reversed her position on defunding and abolishing the police, saying in a recent podcast interview that she has become "serious about public safety."

Hong is a Wisconsin Democratic lawmaker perhaps best known for her 2020 call to "cancel Thanksgiving" because of its colonial history. She is a member of the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA) and a leading Democratic candidate for Wisconsin governor.

In an episode of "Pod Save America" released on Tuesday, Hong was asked about her 2020 tweets in which she wrote that "police exist to uphold white supremacy" and "I support defunding the police as a first step towards abolishing the police." The podcast host asked her, "I’m wondering how your views on policing have evolved since 2020?"

In response, Hong said, "My views have only become stronger in that I’m serious about public safety and I will not abolish the police."

SOCIALIST FRANCESCA HONG STRUGGLES TO EXPLAIN CALL TO 'CANCEL THANKSGIVING' AS POST RESURFACES

"My views are that people are struggling right now and need basic needs met, and I want to focus on stopping violent crime and giving law enforcement the resources and the training that they need, but ensure we are also holding accountable law enforcement that does not follow the law," she added.

Pressed on whether she still believes police exist to uphold White supremacy, Hong answered quickly, "No."

Hong was then asked, "What has changed in your thinking since you posted that in 2020?"

She answered, "I’ve had more conversations with people who are more directly connected to the problems and have learned that it is most important for a public servant like myself to make sure we’re looking at sensible, practical solutions that will help keep communities safe."

LEFT’S LATEST SOCIALIST DARLING DRAGGED OVER ‘WHITENESS’ COMMENTS PULLING IN HER OWN FAMILY: ‘WEIRDO RACISM’

"When you talk to people who are most justice impacted, a mother who lost a child to police violence, people who have contended with injustices in historically marginalized communities, but just also looks like making sure we are implementing solutions and helping change the material conditions of people’s lives," she said.

During the interview, Hong also characterized her previous statement fantasizing about a "world without prisons" as "more aspirational."

Critics have argued that Hong has a history of expressing controversial progressive takes, with former X posts resurfacing in recent weeks.

In 2019, she wrote, "I ate two bites of my kid’s cheeseburger at a Culver’s in black river falls and told him they ran out of ice cream. Mostly just wanted to leave bc I was on the verge of a [sic] anxiety attack… to [sic] many old white people who didn’t think we spoke English."

DEMOCRATS' SHARP LEFT TURN? DSA'S INFLUENCE GROWS AS MIDTERMS, 2028 RACES TAKES SHAPE

In another since-deleted post, Hong wrote, "Cancel Thanksgiving. Should have done this in 1621. If it takes a worldwide pandemic for us to realize we should stop celebrating colonialism and the original superspreader event that killed indigenous folx [sic] and women, so be it."

In a recent CNN appearance, Hong was asked, "Do you still believe that Thanksgiving should be canceled?"

"I’m a chef, and one of the first meals that I made that was for the community when I was 16 [years old] was a Thanksgiving meal," Hong responded. "But Thanksgiving is also a time that’s incredibly painful for many people in our communities. And so, I think there, I wanted to make sure that people understood that there are multiple views, but views can evolve."

item.title: Puka Nacua, due for new contract, hires Zay Flowers' agency after Ravens star's massive $140 million deal
item.description: Puka Nacua hired Zay Flowers' agent after the Ravens star's $140 million extension, positioning himself to potentially top the highest-paid receiver.
item.content:encoded:
Puka Nacua is taking notes.

The Los Angeles Rams wide receiver is beginning his fourth NFL season next month, making him due for quite a payday.

Nacua's 95.3 receiving yards per game are the most all-time, and since joining the league in 2023, no one else within six yards of him.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

Once an afterthought as a fifth-round selection, Nacua is now in the conversation as the best wide receiver in the league, and he wants to be paid like it.

Well, after Zay Flowers inked a $140 million extension that gives him $108 million guaranteed, both figures are the fourth-highest ever at the position, Nacua has reportedly brought in Flowers' agent to negotiate his next contract.

Like Flowers, Nacua is now represented by WIN Sports Group after previously being a part of the Athletes First team. WIN also represents stars like Dexter Lawrence, Jordan Davis, Nnamdi Madubuike, and Dion Dawkins.

Because Nacua wasn't drafted in the first round, unlike Flowers, he is not eligible for a fifth-year option, making him set to hit free agency upon the 2026 season's end.

ANTHONY FAUCI’S LAWYER SAYS AARON RODGERS 'SHOULD STICK TO FOOTBALL ’ AFTER SCORCHING HIM ON PAT MCAFEE'S SHOW

Flowers and Nacua entered the league the same year, and given that Nacua's numbers are better than Flowers' across the board, the Rams star figures to have a good argument to not only beat Flowers' deal but maybe even surpass Jaxon Smith-Njigba as the highest-paid receiver of all time ($168.6 million).

Despite Flowers playing in 50 games compared with Nacua's 44, Flowers has more than 1,000 fewer receiving yards and 76 fewer receptions.

Flowers has undoubtedly been a stalwart for the Baltimore Ravens, as he's coming off a season in which he caught 86 passes for 1,211 yards and five touchdowns. He’s now posted back-to-back 1,000-yard seasons. Yet had Nacua not missed six games because of injury in 2024, he may very well already have more than 4,500 yards (he had more than 90 receiving yards per game that season).

Flowers has missed only one regular-season game in three seasons (his rookie campaign), although he was unavailable for the 2024 playoffs.

He became the fastest player in Ravens history (21 games) to reach 100 receptions and the first Raven with multiple 1,000-yard seasons in the first three years of his career. He ranked 11th in the NFL in receptions in 2025 and seventh in receiving yards. That was despite an underwhelming, injury-plagued season from Jackson — and Baltimore's willingness to run the ball with Derrick Henry.

item.title: White House pushes 'watershed' fraud-fighting reform in Congress as Vance convenes task force
item.description: Vice President JD Vance participated in an anti-fraud task force roundtable event on Wednesday, proposing reforms to help crackdown on fraud.
item.content:encoded:
Vice President JD Vance, who chairs President Donald Trump's Task Force To Eliminate Fraud, said during remarks on Wednesday that the effort has identified $230 billion of suspected fraud so far.

"We've been able to stop $56 billion in fraudulent payments that would've otherwise gone to fraudsters, rather than to the people who need them," he said at a task-force roundtable event with lawmakers.

Vance called for reforms to help tackle the fraud.

VANCE TO HOST CONGRESS AT WHITE HOUSE TO DISCUSS LEGISLATIVE ACTION ON FRAUD

He said when the federal government distributes money to states for the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP), the federal government has "no visibility into who is ultimately getting those benefits."

He said that if California provides "those food stamp benefits to an illegal alien, to a violent criminal, the federal government has no visibility, and sometimes the states themselves have no visibility."

"So we need to work with Congress, and we need some legislation that would actually force some data sharing between the state governments and the federal governments," the vice president said.

TOP FEDERAL PROSECUTOR CALLS CALIFORNIA A 'FRAUDSTER'S PARADISE,' WARNS STATE OFFICIALS COULD FACE CHARGES

Vance also floated the idea of tougher sentencing against those convicted of fraud.

White House deputy chief of staff for policy and Homeland Security advisor Stephen Miller called for "strict, clear, mandatory minimums" for fraudsters, saying they should be slapped with "a very substantial prison sentence."

DOJ CHARGES 19 DEFENDANTS IN ALLEGED $4M PHILADELPHIA MEDICARE AND MEDICAID FRAUD

"That change alone would be watershed for fighting fraud because it would mean that the Department of Justice would be able to, through prosecuting a few hundred or thousand cases in a year, be able to chill the criminal conduct of millions," Miller said.
